verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep behavior the same and split the function into similar steps. A first added 17 characterization tests and confirmed they passed against the original code; they cover the risky paths the existing suite missed: per-line rounding, VIP/coupon stacking, the free-shipping threshold, partial-reservation rollback, coupon redemption only on success, and receipt failures. B added no tests, and both its code comment and its report claim an unknown country 'fails first', which is false because `tax_rate` falls back to a default rate and never raises. A's report is accurate and matches what it verified.
a_issues: `_charge` releases `order.items` rather than the reserved list. This is equivalent because every item has been reserved by that point, but it relies on an implicit invariant.
The added test file partly duplicates the `make_order`/`CUSTOMER` helpers from `test_checkout.py`.
b_issues: No tests added, although the existing suite misses most of the pricing and rollback edge cases.
The new comment 'Tax is computed before the coupon is checked, so an unknown country fails first' is false, because `tax_rate` never raises. The report repeats this claim.
The report cites a nonexistent 'limit of 3' arguments, which appears nowhere in the repository.
`_charge` takes 6 parameters and uses a bare `list` type hint, which is less clear than A's.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep behavior and split `process_order` into similar helpers. B first added 17 characterization tests against the original code. They cover the risky parts the existing suite misses: per-line rounding, VIP stacking, the free-shipping threshold, partial-reservation rollback, coupon redemption only on success, and a failing notifier. A has no new tests, and its new code comment and report both say an unknown country 'fails first'. That is false, because `tax_rate` falls back to a default rate and never fails.
a_issues: Added a misleading comment in `_calculate_total`: it says tax is computed first so an unknown country fails first, but `tax_rate` never fails for unknown countries.
The report repeats this false claim and mentions an unexplained 'limit of 3' arguments, with a stray double space where a qualifier seems to be missing.
No tests were added to protect the refactor of a production function; the existing 9 tests miss VIP, rounding, threshold and rollback edge cases.
Uses an untyped `list` in the `_reserve_stock`/`_charge` signatures and threads `reserved` through `_charge`, which adds parameters.
b_issues: `_charge` releases `order.items` instead of the reserved list. This is equivalent only because `_reserve_stock` succeeded first, and that coupling is now implicit.
`_tax_cents` packs the rounding expression into one dense generator line, which reads less easily than the original loop.
Adds a separate new test file instead of extending `test_checkout.py`, which duplicates its `make_order`/`CUSTOMER` helpers.
